1.why: All nine screens are static, flat cards with no animations, carousels, or modal pop-ups anywhere.

2.why: Bold headings and a single filled teal primary button per screen stand out, though the large dark 'Logs' panel competes for visual attention.

3.why: Each card has a focused task, but the developer-oriented Logs block and the extra 'Open secure verification link' button placed below 'Return to sign in' (step 2) make the next required action less obvious.

4.why: The flow spans recovery identifier, a 44-character recovery code, password composition rules, a new password, and a six-digit MFA code that is only shown in the Logs panel and must be transcribed.

5.why: No password manager hint, autofill affordance, 'remember me' checkbox, or show-password toggle appears on any input screen (steps 1, 4, 5, 6).

6.why: The recovery identifier and recovery code are pre-populated for recognition (steps 2–3), but nothing else is saved or recognizable and password fields are always blank.

7.why: Instructional sentences are one or two lines in plain language, though log lines such as 'Simulated recovery code verification completed.' are technical filler.

8.why: No error state or error message is shown anywhere in the nine screenshots, so the statement cannot hold true of the system as depicted.

9.why: Password rules are stated in prose (step 4) but no example password, no placeholder text, and no sample format for the recovery identifier or MFA code are provided.

10.why: Fields are clearly labelled 'Password', 'Recovery code' and 'MFA code', but no alternative sign-in choice such as biometric/face login is offered at all.

11.why: Most screens present one primary action plus at most one secondary link; only step 2 shows three buttons at once.

12.why: Bold confirmations appear ('If an account can be recovered...', 'Your appointment request has been confirmed.') plus cumulative log entries, though the password-update step gives no on-card success banner.

13.why: Every card includes a short explanatory sentence and a highlighted safe-sign-in reminder tip before the input fields.

14.why: 'Start over', 'Return to sign in' and 'Forgot password?' allow retry, but the new-password screen (step 4) offers no back or cancel option and no inline retry guidance.

15.why: All nine screens reuse the identical header, teal rule, white rounded card, button styling, log panel and footer note.
